title: Ceva Condition: d·e·f = (1-d)·(1-e)·(1-f)
content: cevaCondition d e f formalizes the algebraic criterion for cevian concurrency: d·e·f = (1-d)·(1-e)·(1-f), where d, e, f ∈ (0,1) are the affine parameters of cevian points D on BC, E on CA, F on AB. The classical signed-ratio form is BD/DC · CE/EA · AF/FB = 1; translating: BD/DC = d/(1-d), so the product = d·e·f/((1-d)(1-e)(1-f)) = 1 iff d·e·f = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f). The symmetric form makes the condition easy to check: for medians d=e=f=1/2, both sides equal 1/8.
mathContext:
d = BD/(BC),\; e = CE/(CA),\; f = AF/(AB)\\
\frac{d}{1-d} \cdot \frac{e}{1-e} \cdot \frac{f}{1-f} = 1 \iff d \cdot e \cdot f = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f)\\
\text{Medians: } d=e=f=1/2 \Rightarrow \tfrac{1}{8}=\tfrac{1}{8} \checkmark

title: Explicit Concurrency Point: ((1-d)(1-e)/w, d(1-e)/w) where w = 1-e+de
content: cevaConcurrencyPoint gives the explicit coordinates of the intersection of cevians AD and BE for the standard triangle A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(0,1). Line AD parametrized as (s(1-d), sd); line BE as (1-t, t(1-e)). Solving: s(1-d) = 1-t and sd = t(1-e) gives s = (1-e)/w where w = 1-e+de. The concurrency point is ((1-d)(1-e)/w, d(1-e)/w). w_pos (line 167) proves w > 0 from d,e ∈ (0,1) via nlinarith, guaranteeing well-definedness. The third cevian CF passes through this point precisely when the Ceva condition holds, proved in concurrency_on_CF via nlinarith on the Ceva identity.
mathContext:
w = 1 - e + de > 0 \quad (d,e \in (0,1))\\
P = \left(\frac{(1-d)(1-e)}{w},\; \frac{d(1-e)}{w}\right) = AD \cap BE\\
P \in CF \iff d \cdot e \cdot f = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f)

title: Forward Direction: Ceva Condition Implies Concurrency
content: ceva_geometric_standard is the main forward theorem: the Ceva condition implies the three cevians AD, BE, CF of the standard triangle A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(0,1) are concurrent. The proof supplies cevaConcurrencyPoint as the explicit witness: it lies on AD (concurrency_on_AD) and BE (concurrency_on_BE) by construction; it lies on CF (concurrency_on_CF) exactly when the Ceva condition holds. The proof of concurrency_on_CF uses the parameter u = (1-d)(1-e)/(f·w) and nlinarith combining hceva and w_pos to verify the second coordinate identity.

title: Converse: Concurrency Implies Ceva via System of Line-Parameter Equations
content: ceva_converse_standard proves the converse: if all three cevians share a common point P, then d·e·f = (1-d)·(1-e)·(1-f). The proof destructures the areConcurrent hypothesis to obtain line parameters (s, t, u) at P, derives equations (hP1_AD, hP2_AD, etc.) via linarith, then extracts two key constraints: (1) u·f·d = (1-u)·(1-d) (from P on AD and CF), (2) u·(1-f+e·f) = e (from P on BE and CF). Combined via nlinarith with the positivity 1-f+ef > 0, these give d·e·f = (1-d)·(1-e)·(1-f). The long inline comment traces the algebraic derivation explicitly.
mathContext:
P \in AD \cap BE \cap CF \Rightarrow d \cdot e \cdot f = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f)\\
\text{From line params: } u \cdot fd = (1-u)(1-d) \text{ and } u(1-f+ef) = e\\
\text{Cross-multiply: } efd = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f)

title: AffineMap2D: Invertible Affine Maps Preserve Cevian Concurrency
content: AffineMap2D (line 381) is a 2×2 affine map with matrix (a₁₁ a₁₂; a₂₁ a₂₂) and translation. affine_preserves_line (line 403) proves that injective affine maps preserve collinearity (P ∈ lineThrough A B → M(P) ∈ lineThrough M(A) M(B)), proved by exhibiting the same parameter t. affine_preserves_concurrency (line 414) lifts this to concurrency by applying affine_preserves_line three times to the witness. stdToTriangle (line 433) sends the standard triangle to any (A,B,C) with determinant = signedArea(A,B,C) (proved via stdToTriangle_det). The non-degeneracy condition triangleNonDegenerate ↔ det ≠ 0 allows reduction of the general case to the standard one.

title: Angle Bisectors Concurrent: Incenter via Ceva's Theorem
content: angle_bisectors_concurrent (line 754) proves the angle bisectors of any non-degenerate triangle with side lengths a, b, c > 0 are concurrent — the incenter exists — via Ceva's theorem. The angle bisector to side a divides the opposite side in ratio b:c (angle bisector theorem), giving cevian parameter d = b/(a+b), e = c/(b+c), f = a/(c+a). angle_bisectors_ceva (line 729) verifies the Ceva condition: d·e·f = abc/((a+b)(b+c)(c+a)) = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f). angle_bisector_param_pos (line 739) proves d, e, f ∈ (0,1) from a, b, c > 0 so ceva_iff_general applies.

title: Routh's Theorem: Inner Triangle Area = 1/7 at d=e=f=1/3
content: routhRatio (line 838) defines R(d,e,f) = (d·e·f - (1-d)(1-e)(1-f))² / ((1-d+de)(1-e+ef)(1-f+fd)) — the ratio of the inner triangle area (formed by the three cevians) to the original triangle area. routh_zero_iff_ceva (line 844) proves R = 0 iff the Ceva condition holds: when the cevians are concurrent, the inner triangle degenerates to a point. routh_medial_thirds (line 871) proves the famous 1/7 result: at d=e=f=1/3, the three cevians divide the triangle into seven regions of equal area, with the inner triangle having area = 1/7 of the whole. This is a celebrated combinatorial geometry fact.
